newsitem.title: USA: America Online asks court to allow junk e-mail ban.
newsitem.headline: America Online asks court to allow junk e-mail ban.

text.p: America Online asked a federal appeals court on Friday to lift an injunction that forbids it from blocking a Philadelphia marketing firm's "junk" e-mail flooding its subscribers' electronic mailboxes.
The Dulles, Virginia, company, the nation's largest provider of online services, said it had blocked five sites Sept. 5 serving as clearinghouses for unsolicited, commerical mailings.

The next day, senior U.S. District Judge Charles Weiner ordered AOL to lift the restriction on Cyber Promotions' mailings pending a Nov. 12 trial of a lawsuit the company filed in March accusing AOL of trying to drive it out of business.

Cyper Promotions Inc. controls three of the five sites blocked by AOL. The others -- one that distributed software to create bulk e-mail lists and another that sent out ads for Internet video pornography -- were not affected by Weiner's three-paragraph order.
AOL has asked for a hearing before a three-judge panel of the Third U.S. Circuit Court of Appeals, seeking to have the injunction lifted.
Court papers filed Friday gave no details about the arguments AOL intends to make, but the case is expected to be put on the fast track with legal briefs filed in the next few weeks.
